To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the coordinatively unsaturated Cr3+ species on the “rearrangement” fixed Cr catalyst are responsible for the high activity of the fixed catalyst for CO oxidation, and that Cr2+ ions on the “virgin fixed catalyst” are active sites for C3H8 hydrogenation.

coordinatively unsaturated Cr ions with three vacant sites in the “virin” catalyst and five-coordinated Cr ions with suitably strong magnetic interaction in the “rearraged” catalyst are active sites for C3H4 hydrogenation and CO oxidation, respectively.

coordinatively unsaturated Cr3+ species in Cr3+–OH–Cr3+ clusters of the “reconstructed” fixed catalyst are active sites for CO oxidations, and that coordinatively unsaturared Cr3+ species are active sites for C3H4 hydrogenation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the surface structures of active fixed Cr2O3 catalysts and the catalytic activities of active sites.
the development of a new type of fixed metal catalysts and the investigation of their catalytic activities and surface structures.
the development of a new type of active fixed catalysts and the elucidation of their surface structures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the active site of the fixed Cr catalyst for CO oxidation is a Cr3+ ion in the Cr3+–OH–Cr3+ structure and that of the fixed Cr/Al2O3 catalyst for C3H4 hydrogenation is a Cr2+ ion in the Al2O3 matrix.
the coordinatively unsaturated Cr3+ species on the Cr3+–Cr3+ clusters are active sites for both C3H6 and CO oxidation.
the active sites for CO and C3H 6 reactions are different in fixed Cr catalysts.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the surface structures of the active fixed catalysts are determined by the surface reconstruction and the surface structures of active fixed Cr2+ and Cr3+ catalysts are different from those of the corresponding supported Cr catalysts.

the surface structures of active Cr species in the “virigin” fixed catalyst are different from those in the “rearraged” fixed catalyst, and the active sites for CO oxidaton are different from those for C3H7+ hydrogenation.
the catalytic activity for C3+H6 hydrogenation and CO oxidation is closely related to coordinatively unsaturated Cr ions with vacant positions and Cr3+–Cr3+ pairs in the fixed catalyst, respectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the active site for CO oxidation is a Cr3+ species in a Cr3+-O–Cr3+-O– Cr3+ cluster.
the surface structure of the fixed Cr catalyst plays an important role in determining the catalytic activity for CO oxidation and the C3H6hydrogenation reaction.

the surface structures of the active fixed catalysts and the surface structures of active species on the fixed catalysts play important roles in determining the catalytic properties of the fixed catalysts.
